title: TicketTimingSummary
description: Derived, per-ticket record computed by a downstream consumer of the ServiceTimingEvent stream (not emitted directly by an edge device). One summary per ticket, updated/finalized as later-stage events arrive. Consumed by the anomaly/causal engine as a feature record and by the digital twin for current kitchen-load state.

source_id.description: Identifier of the aggregating consumer, e.g. 'timing-aggregator-01'.

computed_at.description: When this summary was generated or last recomputed. Distinct from the underlying event timestamps.

picked_up_time.description: Timestamp the server took the plate from the pass.

time_to_cook_start_ms.description: order_time -> cook_started_time. Null until both timestamps are present.

cook_duration_ms.description: cook_started_time -> plated_time. The requested 'how long it took to cook' metric.

pickup_delay_ms.description: plated_time -> picked_up_time. The requested 'how long before the server picked it up after it was cooked' metric. This is the field most directly relevant to a food-sitting/quality-at-serve risk signal, and to staffing-load anomaly detection.

total_ticket_duration_ms.description: order_time -> delivered_time (or -> picked_up_time if delivered_time is not yet known).

origin.description: Where the ticket came from. 'interactive' if any event on the ticket has source_kind 'player' or 'crew' (a human-driven session and its automated crew); otherwise the events' own source_kind ('simulated' or 'vendor_integration'). Consumers that build baselines from these summaries keep 'interactive' tickets out of the baseline for the others: they run at a different pace and volume. Added 2026-09-21.

is_complete.description: True only once delivered_time is populated. Consumers should treat an incomplete summary's duration fields as provisional and expect a later update with the same summary_id.
